new.title: Cross the Seljuk pointed-arch Şeytan Bridge at Kahta
new.desc: The Seljuk bridge, known locally as the Devil's Bridge, spans the Kahta Çayı (ancient Nymphaios) within the boundary of Kocahisar, south of Yenikale. It is a single pointed arch of cut stone.
new.tip: Visit together with Eski Kahta Castle and Arsameia, which are close by.

new.title: Look over the Euphrates from Gerger Castle
new.desc: The castle stands on steep cliffs above the Euphrates in Oymaklı village. Cisterns, towers and foundations survive from a Commagene fortress that guarded the kingdom's eastern border and the river crossings, repaired in Roman, Seljuk and Ottoman times.
new.tip: Access is rough and the site is little developed, so wear proper shoes and ask in Gerger town for directions.

new.title: Watch birds at the Gölbaşı Lakes nature park
new.desc: The Gölbaşı lakes (İnekli, Azaplı and Gölbaşı) form a 2,080 hectare nature park and an Important Bird Area, where studies have recorded 63 to 73 bird species. The park has a bird-watching tower and a viewing terrace.
new.tip: Spring and autumn migration are the best times. Bring binoculars.
